paper_metadata.title: Classical and quantum computing methods for estimating loan-level risk distributions

summary: The paper develops a classical Monte Carlo model for loan-level lifetime default risk and reports that 10,000 simulations produce smooth distributions, while only 50 simulations already estimate the distribution in 1.9 s for one account. On the quantum side, it proposes a gate-based QAE approach with quadratic sample complexity O(sqrt(M)) for a simplified unconditional PD model, but concludes that the full competing-risks version would require roughly 4Nm qubits and is beyond near-term hardware.

experiments.description: Quantum Monte Carlo / quantum amplitude estimation for estimating the 95th percentile of lifetime probability of default under a simplified unconditional default-probability model.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Monte Carlo simulation with Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) following Egger et al. / Woerner & Egger

hyperparameters.distribution_assumption: logit-normal approximated by normal/lognormal for efficient loading

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each forecast-horizon unconditional PD distribution UPD(t) is loaded into an m-qubit register; N time-step registers are summed to form lifetime PD; a condition qubit marks whether the sum exceeds a threshold x for QAE.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the cumulative probability a = P(LPD <= x) and invert via bisection to find x at the desired confidence level (95th percentile of lifetime PD).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Threshold test qubit in operator C; no explicit penalty formulation.

problem_instance.description: Freddie Mac mortgage loan-level risk distribution estimation using unconditional default probabilities over a 36-month forecast horizon for selected test accounts.

dataset_specification.description: 30-year fixed-rate conforming mortgages; account-level fields include balance, delinquency, payments, payoff, origination date, score, postal code, LTV, DTI, borrowers, property type, purpose

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Multihorizon survival model and APC decomposition used to generate unconditional PD distributions; logit-normal distributions approximated by lognormal/normal for efficient loading; 10,000 classical Monte Carlo samples used to validate distributional shape.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Proof-of-principle comparison to classical Monte Carlo; 10,000 simulations for distribution plots; fit assessed with Cullen-Frey plot and Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Cramer-von Mises, and Anderson-Darling tests.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical Monte Carlo simulation on CPU
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: APC decomposition; multihorizon survival model; Ornstein-Uhlenbeck extrapolation of environment function; lognormal fit to simulated lifetime PD distributions.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Distribution fitting and goodness-of-fit testing; estimation of mean/variance and confidence intervals.
implementation_details.total_execution_time: 1.9 s for M=50 classical Monte Carlo simulations; 10,000 simulations used for smooth plots

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum amplitude estimation applied to the simplified unconditional lifetime PD estimation problem
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the speed enhancement is on the order of the square root of the number of simulations needed; no hardware experiment was run.

speedup_claims.conditions: when estimating the 95th percentile / confidence interval via QAE
speedup_claims.caveats: Requires a unitary A = USC construction and a threshold test qubit; only a proof-of-principle formulation is given.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M) samples for Monte Carlo estimation; classical error convergence O(1/sqrt(M))

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; the paper states the full competing-risks version would require far more qubits than available in the next couple of years.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: A gate-based QAE circuit with N m-qubit registers plus support qubits; the paper gives no concrete qubit count for the simplified case and notes the full conditional version would need about 4Nm qubits.
limiting_factors: State preparation/loading of distributions is non-trivial
Full conditional competing-risks version requires too many qubits
Current hardware noise/decoherence not addressed experimentally

notes: No actual quantum hardware experiment was run; the paper presents a theoretical gate-based QAE formulation only.
num_qubits is inferred from the paper's statement that N separate m-qubit registers are needed, with additional support qubits, but no numeric qubit count is given.
circuit depth is not numerically reported; only the algorithmic structure U-S-C and QAE are described.
The paper presents a theoretical QAE-based speedup claim relative to classical Monte Carlo, but no quantum benchmark is run.
The authors explicitly say the problem is beyond current quantum computers and that the full competing-risks approach is not feasible in the near term.

experiments.description: Quantum Monte Carlo / QAE for the simplified unconditional PD model, emphasizing efficient loading of log-concave approximations and in-place summation of horizon distributions.

algorithm.variant: Quantum risk analysis / QAE for unconditional lifetime PD with Grover-Rudolph state preparation

hyperparameters.distribution_loading: efficient loading via Grover-Rudolph for log-concave distributions
hyperparameters.target_metric: mean and variance of final distribution parameters
hyperparameters.QAE_precision: improves with number of quantum samples M

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One m-qubit register per forecast horizon; distributions loaded into registers and summed in-place; amplitude estimation used to estimate distribution parameters rather than full histogram.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate mean and variance of the lifetime PD distribution to parameterize a lognormal approximation.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints beyond thresholding in QAE and in-place summation.

problem_instance.description: Same Freddie Mac mortgage unconditional PD forecasting problem, but framed as parameter estimation for a lognormal approximation to the lifetime PD distribution.

dataset_specification.description: Mortgage account-level data with origination and performance attributes

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Use of logit-normal distributions in log-odds space; approximation by lognormal distributions to enable efficient quantum loading.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical complexity comparison only; no hardware benchmark.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical Monte Carlo / classical parameter estimation
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Distribution approximation and parameter extraction for lognormal fit.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Closed-form parameter recovery for the assumed distribution family.

speedup_claims.conditions: for QAE-based estimation of the mean and variance of the final lifetime PD distribution under an unconditional model
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes that efficient loading is possible for log-concave distributions, but logit-normal/lognormal are only approximated; no concrete quantum benchmark is reported.

speedup_claims.conditions: when estimating distribution parameters (mean and variance) for a lognormal approximation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper emphasizes that the result is a theoretical formulation and that current hardware is not sufficient for the full problem.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M) samples for Monte Carlo estimation

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; the paper only argues that QAE could estimate mean/variance with O(sqrt(M)) samples.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: N m-qubit registers for horizon distributions plus support qubits; no concrete device or qubit count is reported.
limiting_factors: Efficient loading assumed for approximated distributions
Distribution approximation to lognormal/normal may reduce fidelity to the original model

notes: This is not a separate empirical run; it is a second theoretical gate-based formulation in the discussion section.
The paper does not specify a concrete device, simulator, or transpiled circuit metrics.
